subject: storytime
title: Little Red Riding Hood
about: The old folk tale of the girl in the red hood and the wolf in Grandma's cap, told gently: Grandma hides in her closet, Red calls for help, a woodcutter chases the wolf far away, and nobody is eaten. The famous What big eyes you have lines are perfect for reading with expression, and the story carries a clear safety lesson about staying on the path and not talking to strangers. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, five pages long.
tip: Take turns being Red and the wolf on the big eyes, big ears, big teeth page, then ask what Red should have done in the woods.

book.author: a folk tale from Europe (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: A red hood, a basket, and a wolf in Grandma's cap.

passage.text:
Once there was a girl named Little Red Riding Hood.
She always wore a red cape with a hood.
One day, Mom packed a basket of muffins.
"Take this to Grandma," said Mom.
"She is sick in bed."
"Stay on the path."
"And do not talk to strangers."
"Yes, Mom," said Red.
***
Red went into the woods.
Soon she met a big gray wolf.
"Where are you going?" asked the wolf.
Red forgot what Mom said.
"To see Grandma," she said.
"Pick her some flowers," said the wolf.
So Red left the path to pick flowers.
The wolf ran off to Grandma's house.
***
Grandma looked out her window.
She saw the wolf coming!
She hid in her closet.
The wolf came in.
He put on Grandma's cap.
He got into her bed.
He pulled the covers up to his nose.
Knock, knock!
"Come in, dear," said the wolf.
Red came in with her flowers.
***
"Grandma, what big eyes you have!" said Red.
"All the better to see you with," said the wolf.
"Grandma, what big ears you have!"
"All the better to hear you with."
"Grandma, what big teeth you have!"
Red looked again.
That was not Grandma!
It was the wolf!
"Help, help!" she yelled.
***
A woodcutter was cutting wood near the house.
He heard Red yell and ran in.
The wolf jumped out of bed.
He ran out the door.
The woodcutter chased him far, far away.
The wolf never came back.
Then Grandma came out of her closet.
She was safe!
Red gave her a big hug.
They ate muffins together.
Stay on the path and do not talk to strangers.

cards.q: Who did Red meet in the woods?
cards.note: Red forgot what Mom said and talked to him, and he was a stranger.

cards.q: Where was Red taking the basket?
cards.note: Grandma was sick in bed, so Mom packed a basket of muffins for her.

cards.q: Where did Grandma hide from the wolf?
cards.note: She saw him coming from her window and hid in time; nobody gets eaten in this telling.
He chased the wolf far, far away, and it never came back.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: The basket and Mom's two rules come first: stay on the path, and do not talk to strangers.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: Grandma came out of the closet, and they ate the muffins together.

cards.q: How did Red feel when she saw Grandma was safe?
cards.note: She gave Grandma a big hug; ask how he feels when a scare is over.
Stay on the path and do not talk to strangers; Red's trouble began when she forgot both.
A stranger is anyone he does not know; it is a good moment to name his safe grown-ups.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
